q: The electric field between two oppositely charged parallel plates is uniform.
e: True. The electric field between two oppositely charged parallel plates is uniform. Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q.

q: The force acting upon a unit positive charge between two parallel plates is equal to the electric field intensity $E$.
e: True. The force acting upon a unit positive charge between two parallel plates is equal to the electric field intensity E. Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q.

q: The work done in bringing a unit positive charge from the negative plate to the positive plate against the electric force is $W = Ed$.
e: True. The work done in bringing a unit positive charge from the negative plate to the positive plate against the electric force is W = Ed. Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts.

q: The relation between potential difference and the electric field intensity between two parallel plates is $V = Ed$.
e: True. The relation between potential difference and the electric field intensity between two parallel plates is V = Ed. Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q.

q: The unit of electric field intensity can also be expressed in volt per metre ($\text{V m}^{-1}$).
e: True. The unit of electric field intensity can also be expressed in volt per metre (V m^-1). Electric field at a point is the force per unit positive charge, E = F/q.

q: Parallel charged plates are two parallel metal plates of different sizes, carrying charges of equal magnitude and opposite signs.
e: False. Coulomb's law is K Q1 Q2 / r² along the line joining the charges. The written line says Parallel charged plates are two parallel metal plates of different sizes, carrying charges of equal magnitude and opposite signs.
